items.stem: What is a LAN?
options: A network covering a small geographical area such as one building or site
A single computer connected to the internet
A network covering a country or the world
A network that only uses wireless connections
items.answer: A network covering a small geographical area such as one building or site
items.markingKey: LAN = local area network: small area, infrastructure usually owned by the organisation.

items.stem: Explain two advantages of a client–server network over a peer-to-peer network for an organisation.
items.answer: Centralised security and access control; centralised backups; files stored in one place so easier to manage; better performance for large numbers of users.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per advantage with explanation, max 2 points × 1 + 1 expansion [3]

items.stem: Explain why a small home office might choose a peer-to-peer network.
items.answer: It is cheap to set up with no dedicated server or specialist staff; easy to share a printer and files among a few computers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: no server needed / low cost; 1 mark: simple to set up for few users [2]

items.stem: Atlas Museum has offices in Karachi and two other cities and wants all offices to share one customer database. Identify two services a server could provide here.
items.answer: File server, print server, email server, web server, authentication/login server.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each, max 2 [2]

items.stem: Sunrise Bakery in Kathmandu has 40 staff who share files, printers and an internet connection in one building. (a) State whether this situation needs a LAN or a WAN, giving a reason. (b) Suggest whether thin or thick clients would be more suitable, and why.
items.answer: (a) LAN if a single site; WAN if several sites in different cities must be connected. (b) Thin clients if a reliable server and network exist and central management is wanted; thick clients if users need to work offline or run demanding software.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark: correct choice; 1 mark: reason linked to geographical area [2] (b) 1 mark: choice; 1 mark: reason [2]

items.stem: Eagles Sports Club is moving from five separate offices in Riyadh into one new building and will also open a branch abroad. (a) Describe how a client–server model would improve security. (b) Explain why a WAN is needed to connect the branch abroad.
items.answer: (a) Central user accounts and access rights on the server; central firewall and anti-malware; centralised backups. (b) The branch is far away; a WAN uses public/leased telecommunications infrastructure to connect separate LANs.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per point, max 2 [2] (b) 1 mark: distance; 1 mark: leased/public infrastructure links LANs [2]

items.stem: Explain one disadvantage of using thin clients.
items.answer: They depend completely on the server and network; if the server or connection fails, the clients cannot work. A powerful server and good bandwidth are needed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: dependent on server/network; 1 mark: consequence (cannot work if it fails / needs high bandwidth) [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between a LAN and a WAN in terms of area and ownership of infrastructure.
items.answer: A LAN covers a small area and its cables/devices are owned by the organisation; a WAN covers a large area and usually uses infrastructure leased from telecommunications companies.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: area; 1 mark: ownership [2]

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Explain the difference between a LAN and a WAN in terms of area and ownership of infrastructure. (b) Explain why a small home office might choose a peer-to-peer network.
items.answer: (a) A LAN covers a small area and its cables/devices are owned by the organisation; a WAN covers a large area and usually uses infrastructure leased from telecommunications companies. (b) It is cheap to set up with no dedicated server or specialist staff; easy to share a printer and files among a few computers.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark: area; 1 mark: ownership [2] (b) 1 mark: no server needed / low cost; 1 mark: simple to set up for few users [2]

items.stem: A school wants pupils to log in from any computer and see their own files. Suggest whether thin or thick clients would be more suitable, and why.
items.answer: Thin clients if a reliable server and network exist and central management is wanted; thick clients if users need to work offline or run demanding software.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: choice; 1 mark: reason [2]

items.stem: The managers of Riverside Medical Centre want to replace a peer-to-peer network that has grown to 60 computers. (a) Describe how a client–server model would improve security. (b) Explain why a WAN is needed to connect the branch abroad.
items.answer: (a) Central user accounts and access rights on the server; central firewall and anti-malware; centralised backups. (b) The branch is far away; a WAN uses public/leased telecommunications infrastructure to connect separate LANs.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per point, max 2 [2] (b) 1 mark: distance; 1 mark: leased/public infrastructure links LANs [2]

items.stem: FreshFarm Foods is moving from five separate offices in Bogotá into one new building and will also open a branch abroad. (a) Explain why the peer-to-peer model becomes unsuitable as the network grows. (b) Evaluate the use of thin clients for the office staff.
items.answer: (a) No central security or backups; files spread over many machines; performance falls when peers serve many requests; hard to manage. (b) Lower cost per device and central management/updates; but dependency on server and network, and high bandwidth needed.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per point, max 3 [3] (b) 1 mark advantage, 1 mark disadvantage, 1 mark conclusion [3]

items.stem: In which topology are all devices connected to a single central cable?
items.answer: Bus
items.markingKey: Bus: one backbone cable with terminators at both ends.

items.stem: Explain why a failure of one cable in a star topology does not stop the rest of the network working.
items.answer: Each device has its own cable to the switch; only the device on the broken cable loses its connection.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: separate cable per device; 1 mark: only that device affected [2]

items.stem: Explain one disadvantage of a bus topology.
items.answer: If the main cable fails the whole network stops; performance falls with many devices because only one can transmit at once (collisions).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: single point of failure / collisions; 1 mark: explanation [2]

items.stem: A full mesh network of 12 routers has one more router added. How many extra links are are needed?
items.markingKey: 13×12/2 − 12×11/2 = 78 − 66 = 12 (the new router links to all 12 existing ones) [2]

items.stem: A full mesh network of 10 routers has one more router added. Calculate how many extra links are needed.
items.markingKey: 11×10/2 − 10×9/2 = 55 − 45 = 10 (the new router links to all 10 existing ones) [2]

items.stem: Amara has been asked to write a report for the managers of Harbour Bank. Evaluate the choice of star topology instead of bus topology for the new network at Harbour Bank.
items.answer: Points in favour: cable failure affects only one device; switch sends data only to the intended device so fewer collisions; easy to add devices. Points against / limitations: more cable and a switch are needed so higher cost; the switch is a single point of failure. Conclusion: star is usually preferred because reliability and performance outweigh the cost.
items.markingKey: Up to 3 marks for relevant technical points correctly applied to the scenario; up to 3 marks for developed explanation that weighs both sides and reaches a justified conclusion. Indicative content: cable failure affects only one device; switch sends data only to the intended device so fewer collisions; easy to add devices. / more cable and a switch are needed so higher cost; the switch is a single point of failure. [6]

items.stem: In a star topology, what device is usually at the centre?
items.answer: A switch
items.markingKey: Each device has its own cable to a central switch (or hub).

items.stem: Explain why a mesh topology is used for the internet backbone.
items.answer: There are many alternative routes, so if one link fails data can be re-routed; it is fault-tolerant.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: multiple routes; 1 mark: reliability/fault tolerance [2]

items.stem: Explain two concerns a company might have before moving its data to a public cloud.
items.answer: Security and privacy of data on third-party servers; loss of access if the internet or provider fails; dependence on the provider; legal issues about where data is stored.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per concern with brief explanation, max 2 [2]

items.stem: A star network has 7 computers connected to a central switch. How many cables are needed?
items.markingKey: One cable per computer to the switch: 7 cables; each computer uses 1 [2]

items.stem: A hospital in Santiago needs a network where a single cable fault will not cut off patient monitoring, and is considering cloud storage for records. Explain how a hybrid topology could be used if the organisation has several floors.
items.answer: A star network on each floor, linked by a bus or mesh backbone between floor switches.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: combination; 1 mark: description [2]

items.stem: Which device connects a LAN to the internet and forwards packets between networks?
items.answer: Router
items.markingKey: A router forwards packets between different networks using IP addresses.

items.stem: Describe how CSMA/CD works.
items.answer: A device listens to check the channel is idle before transmitting; while transmitting it monitors for a collision; if a collision is detected it sends a jam signal and waits a random time before trying again.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: listen/sense carrier before sending; 1 mark: collision detected (jam signal); 1 mark: random back-off and retry [3]

items.stem: Explain why fibre-optic cable is used for long-distance network links.
items.answer: Very high bandwidth; little signal loss (attenuation) over long distances so fewer repeaters; not affected by electromagnetic interference.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per point, max 2 [2]

items.stem: Arjun downloads a 375 MB file over a connection with a transfer rate of 100 Mbps. Calculate the time taken, in seconds (1 MB = 8 megabits).
A 200 MB file must be transmitted in 8 seconds. Calculate the minimum transfer rate needed in Mbps (1 MB = 8 megabits).
items.answer: 200 Mbps

items.stem: SkyLink Airways is installing a network in a new building in Manila. The building has a public Wi-Fi area for visitors and a workshop with heavy electrical machinery. (a) Explain why the switch improves performance compared with a hub. (b) Staff upload 100 MB files over a 200 Mbps link. Calculate the upload time in seconds.
items.answer: (a) A switch forwards frames only to the destination port (using MAC addresses) so there is less traffic and fewer collisions. (b) 4 s
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark: only to destination; 1 mark: less traffic/collisions [2] (b) 100 × 8 = 800 Mb [1]; ÷ 200 = 4 s [1] [2]

items.stem: Which device sends a frame only to the device with the matching MAC address within a LAN?
items.answer: Switch
items.markingKey: A switch uses a table of MAC addresses to forward frames only to the destination port.

items.stem: Compare wired and wireless networks in terms of speed and security.
items.answer: Wired is usually faster and more reliable; wireless signals can be intercepted more easily so need strong encryption (WPA2/3) but give mobility.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: speed comparison; 1 mark: security comparison [2]

items.stem: Kwame downloads a 50 MB file over a connection with a transfer rate of 10 Mbps. Calculate the time taken, in seconds (1 MB = 8 megabits).
Chloe downloads a 25 MB file over a connection with a transfer rate of 100 Mbps. Calculate the time taken, in seconds (1 MB = 8 megabits).
items.answer: 2 s

items.stem: Nadia downloads a 20 MB file over a connection with a transfer rate of 16 Mbps. Calculate the time taken, in seconds (1 MB = 8 megabits). In practice 10% of the bandwidth is used by protocol overheads; state the effect on your answer.
items.answer: 10 s; takes longer: 11.1 s
items.markingKey: 20 MB × 8 = 160 megabits [1]; 160 ÷ 16 = 10 s [1]; effective rate reduced so answer adjusted [1] [3]

items.stem: How many bits are in an IPv4 address?
items.markingKey: IPv4: 32 bits written as four denary octets.

items.stem: Explain why private IP addresses can be reused in many different LANs.
items.answer: Private addresses are not routed on the internet; the router uses NAT to share one public address, so the same private range can exist in every LAN.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: private addresses not routable on internet; 1 mark: NAT/router translates to public address [2]

items.stem: Explain why subnetting is used in a large network.
items.answer: It divides the network into smaller sub-networks, reducing broadcast traffic, improving security (separating departments) and making management easier.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per benefit, max 2 [2]

items.stem: A subnet uses the prefix /20. State the subnet mask in dotted denary and calculate the maximum number of hosts on the subnet.
items.markingKey: 20 ones then 12 zeros: 255.255.240.0 [1]; hosts = 2^12 − 2 = 4094 (network and broadcast addresses excluded) [1] [2]

items.stem: A subnet uses the prefix /25. State the subnet mask in dotted denary and calculate the maximum number of hosts on the subnet.
items.markingKey: 25 ones then 7 zeros: 255.255.255.128 [1]; hosts = 2^7 − 2 = 126 (network and broadcast addresses excluded) [1] [2]

items.stem: State whether the IPv4 address 31.184.100.158 is public or private, giving a reason.
items.answer: Public: it is not in any of the private ranges (10.x.x.x, 172.16–31.x.x, 192.168.x.x)
items.markingKey: 1 mark: public; 1 mark: reason [2]

items.stem: GreenLeaf Pharmacy in Cairo has 200 computers on its LAN, divided into departments, and a public website hosted on its own server. (a) The network manager chooses a /28 subnet for each department. Calculate the maximum number of hosts per subnet. (b) Give two benefits of IPv6 over IPv4.
items.answer: (a) 14 (b) Far more addresses (2¹²⁸); no need for NAT; simpler header/built-in security (IPsec), auto-configuration.

items.stem: GreenLeaf Pharmacy in Lagos has 200 computers on its LAN, divided into departments, and a public website hosted on its own server. (a) Describe how a user's browser finds the IP address of the company website. (b) Give two benefits of IPv6 over IPv4.
items.answer: (a) Domain name sent to DNS resolver; looked up / passed up the DNS hierarchy; IP returned to browser which then connects. (b) Far more addresses (2¹²⁸); no need for NAT; simpler header/built-in security (IPsec), auto-configuration.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per step, max 3 [3] (b) 1 mark each, max 2 [2]

items.stem: How many bits are in an IPv6 address?
items.markingKey: IPv6: 128 bits as eight groups of four hex digits.

items.stem: What is the role of a DNS server?
options: To translate a domain name into an IP address
items.answer: To translate a domain name into an IP address
items.markingKey: DNS resolves URLs/domain names (e.g. www.example.com) to IP addresses.

items.stem: Describe the steps taken when a browser uses DNS to find a web page.
items.answer: Browser sends the domain name to a DNS server; if found, the IP address is returned; if not, the request is passed up to other DNS servers; the browser then sends the request to the IP address.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: domain sent to DNS server; 1 mark: lookup/forwarded to other DNS servers; 1 mark: IP returned and used to contact web server [3]

items.markingKey: AND the address with the mask bit by bit: network address 38.67.179.0 [2]

items.stem: Lina is the network manager of Harbour Bank, which has a LAN divided into departmental subnets and its own public web server. (a) Explain why the computers on the LAN can use private IP addresses. (b) The network manager chooses a /26 subnet for each department. Calculate the maximum number of hosts per subnet.

items.stem: Ethan is the network manager of Harbour Bank, which has a LAN divided into departmental subnets and its own public web server. (a) Explain why the web server needs a public static IP address. (b) Describe how a user's browser finds the IP address of the company website.

items.stem: Amara shortens the IPv6 address 8919:a72c:eab3:c5cb:cb7e:fcb0:d100:3544 to 8919:a72c:eab3:c5cb:cb7e:fcb0:d1:3544. Explain the error and give the correct form.
items.answer: Only leading zeros in a group may be removed; trailing zeros are significant, so group d100 becomes d100, not d1. Correct: 8919:a72c:eab3:c5cb:cb7e:fcb0:d100:3544.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: only leading zeros can be omitted; 1 mark: 8919:a72c:eab3:c5cb:cb7e:fcb0:d100:3544 [2]

items.stem: FreshFarm Foods is reviewing its IT infrastructure in Toronto. Assess whether FreshFarm Foods should move all of its data and software to a public cloud.
items.answer: Points in favour: access from any location; no need to buy servers; provider handles backups and maintenance; scalable pay-as-you-go cost. Points against / limitations: security/privacy risk of third-party storage; reliance on internet connection and provider; ongoing subscription costs; legal issues about data location. Conclusion: a hybrid or careful contract may give the benefits while controlling risks.
items.markingKey: Up to 4 marks for relevant technical points correctly applied to the scenario; up to 5 marks for developed explanation that weighs both sides and reaches a justified conclusion. Indicative content: access from any location; no need to buy servers; provider handles backups and maintenance; scalable pay-as-you-go cost. / security/privacy risk of third-party storage; reliance on internet connection and provider; ongoing subscription costs; legal issues about data location. items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) What does CSMA/CD stand for? (b) What is a repeater used for?
items.answer: (a) Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Detection (b) To regenerate a signal so it can travel further
items.markingKey: (a) Used in (shared) Ethernet to detect and recover from collisions. (b) Repeaters boost/regenerate weakened signals over long cable runs.

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) Describe how CSMA/CD works. (b) Explain the difference between a switch and a router.
items.answer: (a) A device listens to check the channel is idle before transmitting; while transmitting it monitors for a collision; if a collision is detected it sends a jam signal and waits a random time before trying again. (b) A switch connects devices within one LAN and forwards frames by MAC address; a router connects different networks and forwards packets by IP address.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark: listen/sense carrier before sending; 1 mark: collision detected (jam signal); 1 mark: random back-off and retry [3] (b) 1 mark: switch within LAN / MAC; 1 mark: router between networks / IP [2]

items.stem: Mohammed downloads a 75 MB file over a connection with a transfer rate of 50 Mbps. Calculate the time taken, in seconds (1 MB = 8 megabits).

A factory owned by City Central Library near Cape Town is being networked; it has a visitor Wi-Fi area and network cables must run past heavy electrical machinery. (a) Identify the hardware needed to connect the wireless devices to the wired network, and to connect the network to the internet. (b) Explain why the switch improves performance compared with a hub.
items.answer: (a) Wireless access point(s); router (with switch for wired devices). (b) A switch forwards frames only to the destination port (using MAC addresses) so there is less traffic and fewer collisions.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark WAP; 1 mark router [2] (b) 1 mark: only to destination; 1 mark: less traffic/collisions [2]

items.stem: Tariq shortens the IPv6 address 93a3:afe7:0000:0000:34c2:22a1:0000:0000 to 93a3:afe7::34c2:22a1::. Explain why this is not valid and give the correct shortest form.
items.answer: "::" may only appear once, otherwise it is impossible to tell how many zero groups each "::" replaces. Correct form: 93a3:afe7::34c2:22a1:0:0.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: :: used only once / ambiguity; 1 mark: longest zero run replaced, other written as 0 groups: 93a3:afe7::34c2:22a1:0:0 [2]

items.stem: Isla shortens the IPv6 address 4d00:41b3:12cb:d564:9c7c:e410:7fb9:2424 to 4d:41b3:12cb:d564:9c7c:e410:7fb9:2424. Explain the error and give the correct form.
items.answer: Only leading zeros in a group may be removed; trailing zeros are significant, so group 4d00 becomes 4d00, not 4d. Correct: 4d00:41b3:12cb:d564:9c7c:e410:7fb9:2424.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: only leading zeros can be omitted; 1 mark: 4d00:41b3:12cb:d564:9c7c:e410:7fb9:2424 [2]

items.stem: Sipho shortens the IPv6 address 3ac4:81f0:fe17:e700:c147:3f58:81bc:fcc8 to 3ac4:81f0:fe17:e7:c147:3f58:81bc:fcc8. Explain the error and give the correct form.
items.answer: Only leading zeros in a group may be removed; trailing zeros are significant, so group e700 becomes e700, not e7. Correct: 3ac4:81f0:fe17:e700:c147:3f58:81bc:fcc8.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: only leading zeros can be omitted; 1 mark: 3ac4:81f0:fe17:e700:c147:3f58:81bc:fcc8 [2]

items.stem: The IPv4 address 127.71.243.208 is stored in binary. Give octet 4 (208) as 8-bit binary.
A subnet uses the prefix /22. State the subnet mask in dotted denary and calculate the maximum number of hosts on the subnet.
items.markingKey: 22 ones then 10 zeros: 255.255.252.0 [1]; hosts = 2^10 − 2 = 1022 (network and broadcast addresses excluded) [1] [2]

items.stem: Horizon Travel in Doha has 200 computers on its LAN, divided into departments, and a public website hosted on its own server. (a) Explain why the computers on the LAN can use private IP addresses. (b) The network manager chooses a /26 subnet for each department. Calculate the maximum number of hosts per subnet.
items.answer: (a) They do not need to be reached directly from the internet; the router uses NAT with a public address. (b) 62
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark: not directly accessed from internet; 1 mark: NAT/router public address [2] (b) 2^6 − 2 = 62 [2]
